audit.whatIsWrong: content win[2] and win[3] give Levels 3 and 4-5 to Volibear, but whys[2] and whys[3] say your Q pattern and drain out-brawl his W lifesteal and your sweetspots keep the edge. win[5] reads Skill at First item while whys[5] says it widens YOUR advantage, and win[6] reads Aatrox while whys[6] says the late game is even.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul is his engine and it needs two casts on the same mark to heal him; Aatrox's Darkin Blade is up every 10s at rank 3 against a 12s Thundering Smash. The packet chart reads Volibear, Volibear, Aatrox, Aatrox, Volibear, Aatrox, Skill — matching the entry's own reasoning. 54.56% over 1787 games.
audit.corrected: Levels 3 and 4-5 to Aatrox, First item to Aatrox, Two+ items evens to Skill; Levels 1-2 and Level 6 stay Volibear.

audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Smash, Frenzied Maul and Stormbringer are all named without cooldowns, so 'bait his Q and re-commit once it's down' has no length attached.
audit.why: Thundering Smash is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, Frenzied Maul a flat 5s, Sky Splitter 16s, Stormbringer 160/135/110. The 12s Q and the 160s R are the two windows the lane is actually played on, and the 5s W is why his healing feels constant.
audit.corrected: 12s Thundering Smash, 5s Frenzied Maul and 160s Stormbringer written into the spikes and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanics are missing and both change how you trade. Frenzied Maul does not heal on cast — it marks the target, and only a SECOND cast on that same target deals bonus damage and heals him. And Thundering Smash does not stun on cast: he gains speed toward you and stuns the first enemy he ATTACKS, so the stun arrives on his auto-attack, not the button.
audit.why: Riot's text: Frenzied Maul — 'Volibear damages an enemy, applying on-hit effects and marking them. Casting this ability again on the same target deals bonus damage and Heals Volibear'; Thundering Smash — 'Volibear gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks.' Breaking away after the first maul denies the heal outright, and the stun is dodgeable by moving out of auto range during the run-up rather than by reacting to a cast.
audit.corrected: Mark-then-second-cast condition on Frenzied Maul and the attack-based stun on Thundering Smash stated in spikes[0], spikes[1], mid and wants.foe[0]. Sky Splitter also noted as shielding him only when he stands in his own blast.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry keeps saying your drain out-heals his W lifesteal and never names anti-heal.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul heals him every second cast on a 5s cooldown and applies on-hit, so his damage rides attack speed from The Relentless Storm rather than raw AD. Grievous Wounds, not armour, is what decides the extended brawl.

edits.before: Level 3 is your first real window — your full Q pattern out-brawls his kit, so land the third-Q knockup to interrupt his W (Frenzied Maul) stacking and drain through his passive shield trades before his level-6 spike.
edits.after: Level 3 is your first real window. Frenzied Maul (5s) only heals him on the SECOND cast into the same mark, so break away after the first one and his sustain never arrives. Knock him up and drain.

edits.before: His level-6 Q-active slow/stun engage plus his all-in tip this window to Volibear; bait his Q (Thundering Smash) knockup by dashing with E and don't trade into it, then re-commit once it's down.
edits.after: Level 6 tips to Volibear. Thundering Smash (12s) stuns on the first enemy he ATTACKS, not on cast — so stay out of auto range during his run-up rather than reacting late, then re-commit in that 12s.

edits.before: After your first bruiser item you take the extended brawl back — your drain plus sweetspots out-heal his W lifesteal and passive shields.
edits.after: After your first bruiser item you take the extended brawl back — but buy Grievous Wounds, since a 5s Frenzied Maul is his sustain engine.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 4-5 are a fight: your Q rotation and drain out-brawl his W lifesteal at 3, and the third-Q knockup interrupts his Frenzied Maul stacking. But level 6 swings back to Volibear — his Thundering Smash knockup-stun into his empowered all-in beats you, so dash it with E or bait it out, then re-spike at your first item where you take the brawl back. Kill him in your windows before his tank items come online.
edits.after: Levels 3 and 4-5 are yours. Frenzied Maul (5s) marks, then heals him only on a second cast into that same mark — leave after the first and he gets nothing. Sky Splitter shields him only if he stands in his own blast, so pull him off it. Level 6 swings back: Thundering Smash (12s) stuns on the first enemy he attacks, so break auto range on the run-up, then re-spike at your first item.

edits.before: Land Thundering Smash (Q) stun to lock your combo
edits.after: Close to auto-attack range on Q so the stun lands

edits.before: Volibear changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Volibear W mark, E, and level 6 dive. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Volibear wants to force long trades, punish overextension, and turn one bad Aatrox cooldown into a lane-losing fight.
edits.after: Volibear changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Frenzied Maul (W, 5s), which marks first and heals him only on the second cast into that mark, and a Thundering Smash that stuns on the first enemy he attacks rather than on cast. Aatrox wins by leaving after the first maul, breaking auto range during the run-up, and buying Grievous Wounds before any long brawl.

edits.before: Volibear W mark, E, and level 6 dive
edits.after: Second Maul on the mark is the heal
